proof_spine: introduce two displayed finite sets and prove their set algebra by extensionality
enumerate first_set to prove that adding one lands in second_set
show a formula-defined function and an anonymous function value
represent the successor relation as a subset of N x N
prove each input has a unique successor output, select it with have fn by exist!, and reconnect it to the graph
show that the formula, anonymous value, and uniquely selected function agree

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm successor_moves_first_set_to_second_set:
    ? forall x first_set:
        x + 1 $in second_set
    by enumerate finite_set:
        ? forall element first_set:
            element + 1 $in {2, 3, 4}
    claim:
        ? forall input first_set:
            input + 1 $in second_set
        input + 1 $in {2, 3, 4}
        input + 1 $in second_set
blocks.reusable_lesson: Enumerate named displayed domains directly; when the codomain is a named alias, keep one explicit literal-to-name membership bridge if final replay needs it.

blocks.accepted_litex:
have fn successor_from_unique_output by exist!:
    ? forall x N:
        exist! y N st {y = x + 1}
    witness exist! y N st {y = x + 1} from x + 1:
        claim:
            ? forall y1, y2 N:
                y1 = x + 1
                y2 = x + 1
                =>:
                    y1 = y2
            y1 = x + 1 = y2
blocks.reusable_lesson: have fn by exist! selects a callable value from a proved parameterized unique-output relation; keep graph membership as its downstream set-theoretic specification when direct graph elimination would bloat uniqueness.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm selected_successor_lies_on_graph:
    ? forall x N:
        (x, successor_from_unique_output(x)) $in successor_graph
    successor_from_unique_output(x) = x + 1
    (x, successor_from_unique_output(x))[2] = successor_from_unique_output(x) = x + 1 = (x, successor_from_unique_output(x))[1] + 1
    by thm set_builder_member((x, successor_from_unique_output(x)), {pair cart(N, N): pair[2] = pair[1] + 1}) => (x, successor_from_unique_output(x)) $in {pair cart(N, N): pair[2] = pair[1] + 1}
    (x, successor_from_unique_output(x)) $in successor_graph
blocks.reusable_lesson: After unique selection, keep the graph theorem separate: it is the downstream specification that reconnects the callable function to the relation set.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm three_successor_presentations_agree:
    ? forall x first_set:
        successor_on_first(x) = successor_as_value(x) = successor_from_unique_output(x)
    successor_on_first(x) = x + 1 = successor_as_value(x)
    successor_as_value(x) = x + 1 = successor_from_unique_output(x)
blocks.reusable_lesson: When several function presentations share one value, prove two pairwise common-value chains and omit the repeated final equality endpoint.
